subject: Post-demo: PII handling & short-log exception request

To: Elena Morales <emorales@medisyshealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: PII handling & short-log exception request

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment:

- Scope: you asked whether Redwood can support an exception for call center PII where session prompts are not retained (0-retention) and only a minimal operational log is kept for troubleshooting.
- Proposed Redwood approach: option to disable long-term request logs for those specific routes; short-term rolling logs (30 days) for aggregated metrics; transient KV caches used only in-memory and wiped on instance restart.
- Questions we left for you: which fields in your payload you consider sensitive PII (examples: full SSN, full DOB, payment PAN). Also whether Medisys requires data residency (US-only) and whether your legal team will want an amendment to the DPA.

Attachments: I’ve included our security questionnaire and a one-page proposed amendment draft for the short-log exception.

Next steps:
1) If you can send a redacted example payload (PII fields masked) we’ll confirm exact config that implements 0-retention for prompts.
2) Marissa (cc) will scope the implementation effort and confirm runbook for on-call access/audit.
3) If Medisys Legal wants the amendment, Rafael will loop in our contracts team and get it routed for signature.

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up tomorrow if that helps — propose 10:00am PT.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

From: Elena Morales <emorales@medisyshealth.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 17:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: PII handling & short-log exception request

Rafael —

Appreciate the recap. High level answers below:

- Sensitive fields: full SSN, full payment card PAN, full patient medical ID (we can provide a redacted sample).
- Residency: must be US-only for this pilot (data-at-rest in US region).
- Legal: they will likely require a one-off DPA addendum for the 0-retention exception and proof we won’t be able to retrieve prompts after processing.

Two follow-ups: can Redwood provide a technical note that explains exactly what "0-retention for prompts" means (e.g., no persisted request bodies, no searchable logs, KV cache not persisted to disk)? Also, we need to understand whether ephemeral logs retained for 30 days will contain any PII or only request IDs and aggregated metrics.

I’ll ask Legal to review the attached amendment draft — CC'd them.

—Elena
Elena Morales
Director, Security & Privacy | Medisys Health
emorales@medisyshealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

On Mon, Mar 22, 2026 at 5:11 PM Elena Morales <emorales@medisyshealth.com> wrote:
> Rafael —
> 
> Appreciate the recap. High level answers below:
> 
> - Sensitive fields: full SSN, full payment card PAN, full patient medical ID (we can provide a redacted sample).
> - Residency: must be US-only for this pilot (data-at-rest in US region).
> - Legal: they will likely require a one-off DPA addendum for the 0-retention exception and proof we won’t be able to retrieve prompts after processing.

Thanks, Elena. Quick technical note from our side so Legal has concrete language:

- "0-retention for prompts" = request payloads for the specified API routes are not written to long-term object storage or any searchable logging pipeline. Payloads are handled in-memory by the inference runtime and any persisted artifacts (metrics, traces) will not include raw request bodies.
- Ephemeral logs (operational) = include only request IDs, timestamps, latency, model variant, and anonymized error codes; no PII fields are stored in these logs. These logs are maintained for up to 30 days and then automatically purged.
- Residency = we can restrict physical storage and backups to our US region (AWS us-east-1).

We’ve attached an engineering spec (encryption-specs-summary.pdf) and a redlined amendment that uses the above language. If Legal is comfortable with the wording, Rafael and I can coordinate a DocuSign route for signatures.

Implementation notes: we estimate config + small runtime guard changes and a brief security review — ~2 weeks to have controls in place for a pilot. If you need faster, we can scope a prioritized patch but will need an exception approval.

Marissa Cole
Head of Product Security | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Medisys Legal <contracts@medisyshealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <emorales@medisyshealth.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: PII handling & short-log exception request

Marissa, Rafael —

Thanks for the clear note. A couple of legal/controls clarifications before we sign:

1) Auditability: even if prompts are not persisted, we need a tamper-evident audit trail that shows who requested the exception and when it was applied. Can Redwood provide an immutable events log (no request bodies) retained for 12 months?
2) Encryption & keys: confirm that any transient data in-memory is processed on instances with full-disk encryption and that keys are customer-scoped or HSM-backed.

If you can confirm those two items in writing and incorporate a brief clause in the amendment, we can proceed to sign. Otherwise Legal will escalate to procurement for a longer review.

Regards,
Medisys Legal (contracts@medisyshealth.com)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Medisys Legal <contracts@medisyshealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <emorales@medisyshealth.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: PII handling & short-log exception request

Hi —

Quick answers and next steps:

- Auditability: yes — we provide an immutable events log that records control changes and exception approvals (no request bodies). Standard retention for those logs can be set to 12 months for compliance review; we will add this as a clause in the amendment.
- Encryption & keys: all instances for the US pilot will use EBS encryption at rest; keys are customer-scoped via KMS with option for BYOK/HSM. I’ve asked our infra team to add the exact KMS key identifiers into the draft amendment.

Next steps:
1) Marissa will update the amendment with the two bullets above and attach the final engineering spec.
2) I’ll open a DocuSign envelope and include the updated amendment plus our standard DPA redline.
3) Elena — once Legal confirms final language we’ll route for signatures and schedule the pilot runbook review.

Estimated timeline: amendment update + DocuSign: 48 hours. Pilot ready-in: ~10 business days after signed amendment.

Thanks all — I’ll follow up with the DocuSign link shortly.
